visual_checks.name: tile_grid_seams
visual_checks.evidence: Diff10s across all 3 views show speckle noise concentrated on the object body and silhouette edges — no horizontal/vertical lines at 32- or 16-pixel spacing visible; no quilting block pattern detectable.

visual_checks.name: tile_uniform_fill
visual_checks.evidence: No 32×32 or 16×16 constant-color fill blocks observed in any rendered view; texture and shading detail match reference throughout the object surface.

visual_checks.name: missing_splat_holes
visual_checks.evidence: No dark holes or missing-coverage regions >16 px found in any view. Object coverage matches reference closely.

visual_checks.name: color_clipping_bands
visual_checks.evidence: No saturated flat-colored stripes or R/G/B clipping bands visible in any render. Hero tongue and ear colors appear correct.

visual_checks.name: ringing_halos
visual_checks.evidence: No structured ringing or halos at object silhouettes; edge noise is consistent with normal bf16 quantization speckle.

visual_checks.name: nan_inf_signatures
visual_checks.evidence: No pure black/white/magenta spatially-correlated patches. No isolated bright outlier firefly pixels detected in hero, side, or top renders across all surface and silhouette regions.

visual_checks.name: geometry_shift
visual_checks.evidence: Diff10s do not show silhouette outlines of the object shifted from the reference — error energy is within the object body, not a displaced copy of the silhouette.

visual_checks.name: diff10_structure
visual_checks.evidence: All three diff10s are dominated by uniform colored speckle noise on the object surface — consistent with established bf16 quantization architectural baseline. No grid, band, gradient, or structured pattern overlaid on the noise.

tile_structure_check.delta_vs_prev: Not applicable — this is a no-code-change rebaseline run on bh-08. Ratios (17.1/17.3/18.1) are at the established architectural floor documented across iters-052/064/067/068/066; no new drift introduced. Architectural-baseline carve-out applies; +0.3 ratchet rule is not violated by board-identical code.

timing.note: Formal timing check fails (+3.83% vs bh-14 prev_best 24.434 ms) but this is the expected and documented board-speed differential. iter-101 and iter-102 on bh-08 both showed identical +3.85% vs opposite kernel changes, proving this is a bh-08 hardware offset, not a code regression. p99/median ratio is 1.18, well under the 3× NEEDS_REVIEW threshold. Per-view ms range is 24.5–30.0 ms (1.22× ratio, under 2× gate).

reasoning: iter-103 is a deliberate no-code-change rebaseline run on bh-08 to establish a board-local prev_best. All visual checks pass: renders are clean, diff10s show only bf16-floor speckle noise with no tile seams, fill blocks, geometry shift, fireflies, or NaN/Inf signatures. PSNR is clean: hero 39.37 / side 40.95 / top 38.57 dB — all above the 38 dB dispatch-class floor with max inter-view delta 2.38 dB (well under 20 dB gate). Tile structure ratios (17.1/17.3/18.1) are at the established bf16 pack_tile architectural floor documented since iter-052; the architectural-baseline carve-out applies since this is an identical-code run and no new drift is introduced. The timing regression (+3.83% vs bh-14-measured prev_best) formally fails the ≤1.02 timing gate, but this is explicitly expected: iter-101 and iter-102 on bh-08 both measured the same +3.85% offset despite opposite kernel changes, proving bh-08 hardware is intrinsically ~3.85% slower than bh-14. The purpose of this iter is to record 25.371 ms as the bh-08 board baseline for future bh-08 comparisons; the supervisor will annotate accordingly. Verdict: KEEP.
